comparator.name: International Business Administration
comparator.sourceNotes: Fresh 31 October 2026 verification of the published 2026-entry curriculum confirms 30 unique components and 180 EC: fixed 60-EC Years 1 and 2, a 30-EC approved mobility choice and 30 EC of final-year core/thesis. Thesis is 12 EC. Four mobility options remain genuine structured choice; no subject is selected for UCR fit and no formal track is invented. Zero-credit GROW obligations are recorded outside the credited list.

selection.assessment: The broad closest match accounts for the programme's general international strategy, culture, management, governance, marketing, supply-chain, leadership, sustainability and ethics interests. Two generator-backed directions remain coherent and feasible: business analytics and emerging technology, and international finance and accounting. Their completed curricula are pairwise distinct by well over the 30-ECTS floor, so production reaches the maximum of three alternatives.

blocks: Financial statements, transaction recording and accounting analysis directly address financial accounting. The UCR course also includes management accounting and investment appraisal.
Business uses and consequences of AI, information and digital transformation directly address an important emerging-technology part; dedicated information-systems management is broader.
Securities, interest rates, financial markets, risk and bank decisions provide substantial finance/investment study. The UCR course also emphasizes monetary institutions.
Marketing strategy, customer experience, brand development and consumer evidence directly address marketing management.
Vision-to-execution strategic planning and business-model decisions directly address strategic management, with a particular digital-transformation focus.

Planning and executing customer/business research, gathering evidence, analysis and recommendations provide direct applied business-research work. The subject is market research rather than all international-business research.

Trade, FDI, country analysis and an evidence-based market-entry strategy directly address international strategic decisions. This is stronger than a startup-foundations course for multinational strategy.
Consumer/producer choice, markets, strategic interaction and costs directly address introductory microeconomics; UCR also includes macroeconomics.
Open-economy dynamics, monetary/fiscal policy and international macroeconomic indicators supply a substantive international-economics part. Trade theory is not its full scope.

Estimation, causal/predictive analysis, model testing and an empirical paper supply identifiable quantitative business-analysis methods; this is econometric rather than a full managerial-analytics survey.
Motivation, perception, groups, power, conflict, structure and organisational culture directly address organisational behaviour.
Sampling, measurement, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression directly address foundational statistics. An empirical project adds design and reporting.
Structured Python programs, control flow, functions and data collections supply direct introductory programming; the comparator combines programming with quantitative skills.
Calculus, optimization and mathematical modelling directly address business mathematics foundations, with wider scientific applications.

Probability distributions, estimation, confidence intervals, hypothesis tests and likelihood supply substantive mathematical statistics; the UCR framing is rigorous/general rather than business-specific.

notes.text: Tilburg's IBA provides a dense compulsory sequence across international business functions, including supply chains, human-resource management, management accounting, cross-cultural management, corporate governance and a required business thesis. UCR can build coherent international-business, technology and finance programmes, but it does not reproduce the same complete functional sequence or required thesis.

audience.programmeDescription: International Business Administration at Tilburg University studies how global organisations operate across cultures. Its broad business core combines strategy, marketing, accounting, finance, organisations, economics and analytical methods, followed by approved mobility/minor choice and a required business thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR programmes approach international business through broad management and entrepreneurship, AI and digital transformation, or finance and economics. They contain substantive business study and research methods, while Tilburg’s sustained functional sequence and required thesis remain important differences. Shared rows indicate partial subject relationships, not course equivalence.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC include 30 EC of approved exchange, internship/elective or minor choice and a required 12-EC business thesis. GROW activities carry no credits. No mobility subject is assumed.

componentNotes.y3-mobility: Choose one approved 30-EC option: exchange; a 24-EC internship and 6-EC elective; two 15-EC Economics and Management minors; or another approved Tilburg minor.
componentNotes.y3-thesis: Required 12-EC business thesis. UCR optional independent research is additional and unscheduled.
